# Am MOD r30d beta4 — synth, Input ROUTE, bootloader exit

> **BETA — r30d-beta4.** Compatibility with other mods and boot menus (Stock, SampQOL, D.S.B, SampleBoot, mpc-boot-thingy) is still being tested. Back up your projects and card first. Items marked *pending* passed host/emulator checks but still need a check on a physical MPC.

For **Akai MPC Sample stock firmware 1.3.0.12**. This release continues r30c-beta1; installed firmware is never rewritten.

![Synth modules](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/raw/main/docs/media/r30d/synth-modules-en.png)

## Fixes in beta4

- **Tidy card root:** the power report and the status markers now live in one folder, `AmMod/` (`AmMod/MPC_POWER_AUDIT.txt`, `AmMod/Status/`), instead of `MPC_POWER_AUDIT.txt` and `MPC_TRIAL_STATUS/` at the card root, so several systems can share a card. The first start removes the old report and the old marker names; your own files are never touched. (Suggested by the SampleBoot author.)
- **SampleBoot 1.0.3 or later** no longer shows card-root settings files such as `mpcqol.conf` inside the mod's folder, so no `ROOT_FILES=""` change is needed; it remains the workaround for older SampleBoot versions.
- **Installer 1.5.1:** the SampleBoot message is now a hint for older versions only. Bug-report logs are also collected from the boot-menu folders and SampleBoot's `last-boot.log`.

## Fixes in beta3

- **SampleBoot:** Am MOD installs to `autorun/mods/AM-Mod/` and starts from the SampleBoot menu. **Exit to bootloader** (Mod Settings → About) now returns to the **SampleBoot menu**, as it does for D.S.B. Checked on a physical MPC.
- **Boot menu art:** the Am MOD logo appears in the SampleBoot carousel (`sampleboot.png`) and on the D.S.B record (`dsb-record.png`); SampleBoot shows the name “Am MOD”.
- **Installer 1.5.1** detects SampleBoot and installs into the right folder. If SampleBoot's `ROOT_FILES` setting shows a card-root file such as `mpcqol.conf` inside `mods/`, Am MOD refuses to start (its sandbox check rejects a writable file from the card); the installer warns, and the fix is `ROOT_FILES=""` in `autorun/sampleboot/sampleboot.conf` (SampQOL then does not see its card-root settings).

## Fixes in beta2

- **USB inputs** (USB, USB L, USB R) now go through the Input track: Input FX, fader, pan and mute apply to them. USB was mislabelled as a different input before, and its signal arrives on a native channel pair the mod did not process.
- **Input list order:** Source, Mode, Monitor, Threshold, Record via, Record track, Record FX, Tuner, MIDI In. **Monitor** has Off / Auto / On for every source and enables Rear monitoring from the Mixer. Record track shows "-" for Master and Input.
- **Pan on K1 of the FX chain** for tracks, the Input track and Master (Pad Bank + K1 resets it to centre). On the Input ROUTE tab K1 = Pan, K2 = Threshold, K3 = Source for every source, Rear included; the L/R pan and level of the Rear channels stay in Rear Routing.
- **Rear mode:** the Mode row for Rear starts in **Stereo** (listed first, the default when you choose Rear) and offers Rear L, Rear R, L+R Split and L+R Mix. The monitor follows the mode: Rear L plays the left jack only, Rear R the right one, the others both. The MPC's physical output-level panel shows the Rear signal.
- D.S.B: the record label under AM Mod now shows the current version.

## Synth (Mixer pad 13)

- **Five modules, nine pages.** Tone (Oscillators, Mixer), Envelope (Amp, Filter envelope), Keys, Filter + LFO, Voices (Voices, Controller). Modules sit on pads 13–16 and 9; **hold Loop and press a pad**, or step with **+ / −**. The **DATA** encoder flips the pages inside a module.
- **More sound.** Second oscillator (wave, mix, semitone, fine), sub oscillator, noise, drive, a separate filter envelope with amount, key tracking, four LFO shapes, bend range, unison with detune and spread, glide, velocity sensitivity.
- **One row of knobs.** K1–K3 hold the frequently used parameter; the rarely used one is on **Shift+K** and is shown above the knob while Shift is held. See the [synth guide](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/main/docs/SYNTH_GUIDE.md) for every page.
- **Keys page = Tune tab.** K1 Transpose16 / Shift Layout, K2 Tonic / Shift Role, K3 Scale / Shift Colour; values read like the Tune tab, e.g. “D# (P)”, “Natural Minor (P)”, “−4 st”.
- **Fader** (Off / Mod / Pitch) is K1 of the Controller page. Parameters such as LFO Depth, Sub, Noise, Drive and Key track read “Off” at zero.
- **Takeover.** The synth's K knobs follow the Parameter takeover mode (Pickup, Scaled, Jump) like the rest of the Mixer.
- Entering the synth in the Mixer clears the track selection; pads 9–12 show the Input track's effects, because the synth is the Input track's source. Pad 14 no longer leaves the synth.
- Thumbnails mirror the pad layout; the big module drawing on the left shows the live waveform, envelope or filter curve.

## Input and recording

- **Shift+Sample opens the Input ROUTE list from every screen** (Seq, Step Edit, compressor, Project), never the stock Input Config. Rows: Source (Mic / Rear / USB / Resample / Synth), Mode (Rear and USB: Stereo, L, R …), Monitor, Threshold, Tuner and record rows. K1 Pan, K2 Threshold, K3 Source; **B2 FX, B3 MIDI In**, Shift+B2 opens the stock screen. The list scrolls and the pad layout stays as you left it.
- **Sample Record:** K1 selects the input Source (including Synth), Shift+K1 the Rear/USB mode. With the **16 Levels** synth keyboard on, the knobs follow the Tune tab (K1 Transpose16 / Layout, K2 Tonic / Role, K3 Scale / Colour) and redraw when Shift is released.
- The synth always follows the master volume; the old *Direct out* and *Mic layer* options are gone. Changing the Input source takes the Input off the synth.

## Piano Roll

- **Area selection:** hold **DATA**, turn the encoder (time) and move the fader (rows); the covered area is selected live. Release DATA to keep it. A short DATA click without movement still selects the note under the cursor (Shift adds).

## Layout swap

- **Layout and Transpose16 swapped** on the Tune tab, the synth Keys page and Sample Record: **K1 = Transpose16, Shift+K1 = Layout**. Resetting the knob follows the new order.

## MIDI

- Global MIDI/synth defaults, a **MIDI Buttons** page (scrolling list, B3 assign, B2 delete/cancel, faders assignable) and a fader MIDI source.
- Controller modifier buttons (for example Shift on a MiniLab) act as plain buttons unless the MPC's own Shift is held, so a keyboard Shift no longer holds the MPC Shift.
- MIDI In from Input Config: B3 / Shift+B2 switch the input mode, Shift+B3 Buttons, Shift+B2 Clear; the MIDI synth list scrolls.

## Effects

- **Henry Skillz** effects HS Saturator, HS Bass Focus and HS Heat (DSP from [hs-mpc-plugins](https://github.com/Holla-Back-Entertainment/hs-mpc-plugins), used with permission), with their own visuals, a page tab strip and a Heat page highlight. Add Effect has an HS author tab and name search (B2). *Pending device check.*

## Bootloader and D.S.B

- **Mod Settings → About → Exit to bootloader** (B3 confirms, B1 cancels) saves a project copy to `Projects/Mod-Exit-Last` and returns to the **D.S.B menu**; without D.S.B the MPC starts stock firmware. See [Boot menus and bootloader exit](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/main/docs/BOOTLOADERS.md).
- **D.S.B state carry-over:** D.S.B's “start OK” marking now reaches the card's real state file, so a healthy Am MOD start is no longer counted as a crash and the menu stops offering Stock after two starts.
- The D.S.B boot journal and the state-fix log are copied beside the mod on the card for diagnostics (`dsb-boot.log`, `dsb-state-fix.log`).
- Fast-boot idea: pick **AM Mod** once in a boot menu and use **Exit to bootloader** whenever you want a different system.

## Other

- Browser search shows a **Find** label; Shift+B2 clears the whole text.
- Synth Hold note holds the last 16 Levels note and shows it highlighted.
- Synth FX tail hold and fade-out remove clicks when notes end.

## Limits

- The synth modules, Input ROUTE, takeover for synth knobs, Piano Roll area selection and the layout swap were finished after the last full device check: *pending* hardware verification.
- To Seq recording of a Mic take may not play the new sample in the sequence in every situation; logs from the device are welcome.
- Exit to bootloader hands over to **D.S.B** only. SampleBoot and mpc-boot-thingy are supported for starting the mod; returning to them from the mod is not implemented.
- Cross-mod Load/Save of Internal projects (Am MOD, Stock, SampQOL) is not fully certified.

See [Known limitations](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/main/docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md), [Installation](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) and the [changelog](https://github.com/AlekseyMalykh/am-mod/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

Plug-and-play card for the **MPC Sample, firmware 1.4.0.7 only**: D.S.B, HS 25, HS Treble Bass and 16 HS effects (official plugins).

Unzip to the root of the SD card and follow `README-INSTALL.txt`. Back up your card first. Taking the card out returns the Sample to stock.

**Pre-release:** the Developer Mode and Enhancements menu steps are taken from Akai's SDK docs and have not been confirmed on a real Sample. The launcher only runs on the exact 1.4.0.7 firmware.

No SampQOL (it doesn't work on 1.4). Other providers' OS can't be added to this card; use a separate card per OS.

Licences: includes third-party parts under GPL-3, AGPL-3 and the JUCE licence; texts are in `DSB-Performance/os/dsb-os/licenses`. To request the corresponding source for the GPL/AGPL parts, open an issue on this repository.

SampQOL OS is by Snare Bes, included with the author's approval; see its licence in `autorun/os/SampQOL-0.4.0/LICENSE.txt`. Boot menu follows SampleBoot by Alessandro D'Esposito (MIT). releases.name: LA Version 2.0G
releases.body:
## LA Version 2.0G

- **USB Indiv Out is eight outputs.** The Layout setting is gone: all eight USB channels are outputs, each a mono channel (1-8) or a stereo pair (1-2, 3-4, 5-6, 7-8). The main mix no longer goes over USB alongside them, so a pad or track on an output is not sent to the computer twice. For the whole song in stereo, use USB Audio Out with USB Indiv Out off.
- **In mix is gone.** The MPC's own line out and headphones always play every track, whether or not it is on an output.

Everything from 2.0A to 2.0F is included.

releases.name: LA Version 2.0F
releases.body:
## LA Version 2.0F

- **Track mute heard at once.** Muting or unmuting a track (Track Mute page, Track Mixer, UNMUTE ALL, and solo) now takes effect immediately. Before, a mute only stopped new notes, so a loop or long sound rang until it ended, and an unmute waited for the track's next note (often the next bar). A muted track now plays its notes unheard, so a loop comes back in where it is. Muted MIDI tracks send nothing.
- **USB Indiv Out: the mix on any pair.** Stereo outputs are 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 or 7-8. Layout: **MIX AUTO + 6 OUTS** (new default) puts the main mix on the first pair nothing else uses and always keeps one pair whole for it (with 1, 3, 5 and 6 taken, 7 and 8 cannot be taken one at a time: the mix plays on 7-8); **MIX on 1-2 / 3-4 / 5-6 / 7-8 + 6 OUTS** fixes it to a pair; **8 OUTS** as before. In use shows the mix's pair as MM.

Everything from 2.0A to 2.0E is included.

releases.name: LA Version 2.0E
releases.body:
## LA Version 2.0E

- **No more held notes in 16 Levels with S600 programs.** With the arpeggiator sliding (Portamento) on a poly S600 sound or in 16 Levels, a slide could move another note sounding on the same pad, and that note never ended (a low held note not otherwise on the pads). Now only the note slid from moves.
- **Also Play notes end.** A pad played through Also Play now ends with the note that started it (S600 sounds hold until released).
- **New project after another program.** LOAD, B1 <New> now switches the pads back to program 1 as well. Before, after using another program (for example a Zone Assign program), a sequence or MPC 2500 project loaded next could have no sounds on its pads.

Everything from 2.0A to 2.0D is included.

releases.body:
## Firmware compatibility — read before updating

> **For Akai MPC Sample firmware 1.3. We strongly recommend staying on firmware 1.3 and NOT updating to firmware 1.4 if you use this GRIDZILLA release.** Firmware 1.4 compatibility has not been verified for this build. Wait for a GRIDZILLA release with confirmed 1.4 support before updating your MPC.

## GRIDZILLA 1.2.9 — Stability Update

GRIDZILLA adds instruments, MIDI editing, song arrangement, mixing and FX automation to the MPC Sample. It runs from the SD card without flashing Akai firmware.

This update adds a clean Master for new songs and brings the Henry Skillz FX collection, selected-pad Melodic editing, sequence looping in Grid and Melodic, a synchronized Loop light, and safer Mixer editing during project loading. The current release passed its hardware qualification, audio checks and normal reboot test on the MPC Sample.

### Updated Mixer and FX

Open the Mixer with **SHIFT + Pad 5**. Select a pad or **MASTER**, open **Inserts**, and choose an empty slot.

**Nine Henry Skillz effects are included:**

- Heat
- Pump
- Bus Compressor
- Channel Strip
- Para EQ
- Tube Strip
- Bass Focus
- Crush
- Saturator

Henry's effects are available on pad and Master inserts. **Flex Beat** is available on pad insert slots; Master inserts use the nine Henry effects. Open an occupied slot to edit it, and use **Next Page** for additional controls while playback continues.

**New empty songs now start with four clear Master insert slots.** Native PAD FX stays available independently of those user slots. Empty slots stay empty after save/reload, and effects already saved in existing projects are preserved. The Flex editor also clears stale Master-effect references during project changes.

The Mixer provides four insert slots, colored meters, pad and Master faders, and SHIFT controls for mute and solo. Faders range from silence to +12 dB, with 0 dB at unity. Existing saved levels are retained.

Henry Skillz's DSP is credited in the included **HENRY-FX-NOTICE.txt**, with its MIT license.

### Loop the sequence you are editing

- Open Grid with **SHIFT + SEQ**, then press **LOOP** to enable or disable looping for that sequence.
- The same control works in **Melodic** mode.
- With Loop enabled, **STOP → PLAY** restarts the sequence you are editing at its loop start.
- **SHIFT + PLAY** retains the native resume behavior, and saved sequence loop boundaries are preserved.
- The **Loop button lights up when looping is enabled** and stays synchronized across modes, including Grid, Melodic, Song, Mixer and Sample.
- The Arranger keeps its own song/cycle loop range.

### Melodic editing and transpose

Melodic mode now shows **only the selected pad's notes**, including their per-note tuning. The pad label identifies what you are editing. Switching pads changes the displayed notes; an empty pad shows an empty view.

Chord selection and transposition apply only to that pad, even when other pads have notes at the same pitch or time. Return to **Grid** to see the complete pattern. Single-note and chord transpose, copy, Undo/Redo, and native save/reload were checked on hardware.

### Instruments, arrangement and automation

- **16 LEVELS** opens the instrument library and chord mode. Play single notes or one-pad chords from triads through 13ths.
- Edit recorded notes in Melodic and change an existing instrument while the Song plays.
- **SNAP** aligns newly recorded note starts to the selected grid; **SNAP OFF** preserves performed timing. Existing notes stay in place.
- Use Grid and Melodic Tools, **ADD SEQUENCE**, and sequence-position controls to build and edit your arrangement.
- Use **TOUCH, LATCH or WRITE** to record FX changes and **READ** to play them back. Flex Beat supports MIX automation and individual ON/OFF points on the grid.
- The stopped-state “STOP” text has been removed from the Arranger bar.

### Stability and hardware verification

Mixer insert, removal, Undo and Redo actions are temporarily unavailable while a project loads, then return when loading finishes. This addresses the identified Mixer load-readiness issue.

Release qualification covers:

- Grid and Melodic Loop on/off, repeated loop playback, Stop/Play restart and cross-mode Loop-light checks.
- Song-to-Grid handoff, repeated sequence occurrences, saved loop bounds and eight reload cycles.
- Selected-pad display, pad switching, chord and single-note transpose, copy, Undo/Redo, and save/reload checks.
- Audio timing and pitch checks.
- Empty Master creation and save/reload, native PAD FX state and playback, and exact preservation of saved Master effects.
- Flex Beat controls, bypass, audio playback, save/reload, removal and Undo/Redo, including use alongside custom Master inserts.
- Ten Henry FX editor cycles, including all 41 Para EQ pages during playback, plus removal and Undo/Redo.
- Normal startup and reboot, with the test device's existing project and musical events preserved.

The Loop, Melodic, controls and Arranger modules retain their previously qualified binaries. The new Master and Mixer changes passed the additional checks above.

**No captured faults occurred in the successful release qualification runs.** Qualification covered the workflows listed above on the tested MPC Sample.

### Download and installation

Download **[GRIDZILLA.zip](https://github.com/ZootedandRebooted/GRIDZILLA/releases/download/GRIDZILLA/GRIDZILLA.zip)** below. This is the tested 1.2.9 Stability Update for an existing supported GRIDZILLA installation on firmware 1.3.

Save your project and back up your SD card before updating. Extract the complete package and follow **INSTALLATION GUIDE.txt** for installation and rollback. Keep `install.sh`, `autorun`, and `WaveGrid` together.

The illustrated **GRIDZILLA-User-Guide.pdf** and **GRIDZILLA-Video.mov** are separate release assets. Use the included installation guide for this update's current instructions.

The ZIP contains runtime files, installation scripts, documentation and license notices. **GRIDZILLA implementation source, development files, credentials and user projects are not included.**

releases.name: Beat-Train v1.6
releases.body:
**Pad sounds.** A song can bring its own drum sounds: one hit per pad colour in a `sounds` folder in the song folder (`kick`, `red`, `yellow`, `blue`, `orange`, `green`, as `.wav`, `.ogg` or `.mp3`). [Trackyard](https://github.com/drose030/trackyard) v1.2.0 lets you pick them from the song's drum track. Turn up **PAD SOUNDS** in the settings and every pad plays its drum's sound, so you hear what you play. The song's own drums keep their volume on SHIFT + K2: all the way down to hear only your playing, or a little under it.

**Quicker sound.** A pad sound now comes out about 12 ms after you hit the pad (it was about 46 ms), with no dropouts on the device.

**The highway no longer looks late.** What the screen shows is always a few milliseconds old. The notes are now drawn that far ahead, so they reach the line when you hear them. The timing offset (K1) can stay at 0.

To update, replace `autorun/beattrain` and `autorun/beattrain.sha256` on your card with the ones from `beattrain-mpc-sample.zip`, or copy the whole `autorun` folder. Your songs and settings in `BeatTrain/` stay as they are.

No songs are included.

releases.name: Beat-Train v1.5

Under the hood, the highway, the song clock, the knobs and fader, and the audio's time stretch were reorganised and are now tested on their own. Playing, the sound and the speed control stay the same.

Install over the old version; your songs, settings and downloaded models stay. The app isn't signed by a registered developer: see the [README](https://github.com/drose030/trackyard#or-the-app-for-mac-or-windows) for the first start.

## New: pad sounds for Beat-Train

Beat-Train can mute the drum stem and play a real drum sound on each pad strike instead. In the editor, the ♪ button right of each row picks that row's sound from the song's own drum stem:

- It steps through the row's hits (‹ › or ←/→), best first: as few other drums at the same time as possible, ringing out freely, no ghost notes. Each one plays, and the cut is marked in its row.
- **Use this** picks it, **No sound** removes it; undo works as for notes.
- Save writes the picks to `sounds/` in the song folder: `kick.wav`, `red.wav`, `yellow.wav`, `blue.wav`, `orange.wav`, `green.wav`, named after the row colours.

A sound starts 1 ms before the hit's attack in the drum stem, found to the sample, and lasts as long as the hit rings, up to the next hit. With pad sounds on, Beat-Train mutes the whole drum stem, so a pad without a sound stays silent. Songs without a drum stem can't get pad sounds.

releases.name: hdslaveOS 0.8.2-hdslave.3 + MPC plug-ins
releases.body:
## Install hdslaveOS on your MPC Sample

**[Download hdslaveOS and all 11 plug-ins in one ZIP](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslaveOS/releases/download/v0.8.2-hdslave.3/hdslaveOS-MPC-Sample-Complete-SD-Card-Install-v0.8.2-hdslave.3-unsigned.zip)**

For a first install, this is the only download you need. Extract it on your computer and open `START-HERE.txt`. The `SD-Card` folder beside it contains the files to copy.

1. **Prepare your MPC and card.** Use firmware **1.3.0.12**, **1.4.0.7**, or **1.4.0.8**. On firmware 1.4, open the stock MPC app’s **Settings → DEV ENHANCEMENTS (BETA)** and turn on **Developer Mode**. Back up the microSD card on your computer.
2. **Copy the OS.** Choose the row for your card. “Top level” means the first window you see when you open the card in Finder or File Explorer.

   | Your card | What to copy |
   | --- | --- |
   | **Regular card (direct boot)** | Move any existing top-level `autorun` folder and `autorun.sh` file to your computer for safekeeping. Open the extracted `SD-Card` folder. Copy **both** the `autorun` folder and the separate `autorun.sh` file to the top level of the card. You should see `autorun.sh` as soon as you open the card. |
   | **Card that already uses SampleBoot** | On the card, create `autorun/mods/hdslaveOS 0.8.2-hdslave.3/`. Open the extracted `SD-Card/autorun/` folder and copy its **contents** there. Check that `autorun.json` sits directly inside the new version folder. Keep the card’s existing top-level launcher. |

3. **Copy the plug-ins.** If the card has no `Melodee` folder, copy `SD-Card/Melodee` to the top level. If it already exists, open or create `Melodee/Plugins/hdslave/` on the card. Copy the **files inside** the extracted `SD-Card/Melodee/Plugins/hdslave/` into that folder, replacing matching plug-in files. Your projects and samples stay in place. Check for `Melodee/Plugins/hdslave/hdslave Nexus.clap` on the card.
4. **Start hdslaveOS.** Eject the card, insert it into the powered-off MPC Sample and turn it on. The stock app appears first. On firmware 1.4, choose **Yes** at the autorun prompt. If you use SampleBoot, turn the encoder to **hdslaveOS 0.8.2-hdslave.3** and push it.
5. **Try a sound.** In hdslaveOS, hold **PAD BANK** and press a pad for an empty track. Choose **Plugin**, open **hdslave**, select **Nexus** and push the encoder. Press **SAMPLE** to open Stage and play a pad.

If the stock app stays on screen, check your firmware and the paths in step 2. If Nexus is missing, check the path in step 3. To boot the stock app again, power off, remove the card and restart.

[Make your first beat with the illustrated quickstart](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslaveOS/blob/v0.8.2-hdslave.3/docs/QUICKSTART.md#4-load-samples-into-a-kit)

### Separate downloads

If you only need one component, use the [OS-only ZIP](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslaveOS/releases/download/v0.8.2-hdslave.3/hdslaveOS-MPC-Sample-SD-Card-Install-v0.8.2-hdslave.3-unsigned.zip) or the [11-plug-in ZIP](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslaveOS/releases/download/v0.8.2-hdslave.3/hdslaveOS-MPC-Sample-11-CLAP-Plugins-v0.8.2-hdslave.3.zip). These ZIPs open directly to `autorun` and `autorun.sh`, or to `Melodee`, respectively. Use the same card destinations above. The `.sha256` files are optional download checks, and GitHub’s source archives are for building from source.

### Slink 0.6.1 for MPC Sample

Both the complete SD-card installer and the separate 11-plug-in ZIP now include **Slink 0.6.1**. Select **hdslave Slink** and open **Stage → Panel** for the wider chrome title and satin-chrome knobs. Existing projects use the same plug-in filename. This refresh updates the plug-in payload and its archive checksums. The OS build is still **0.8.2-hdslave.3**.

![Slink silver panel in Stage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hdslave/hdslave-Slink-Synth/v0.6.1/docs/slink-screen.gif)

[11-plug-in collection release](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslave-MPCSample-Synths-and-Drum-Machines/releases/tag/v0.8.2-slink.2) · [Slink-only download](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslave-Slink-Synth/releases/tag/v0.6.1)

### Reverie 0.6.1

The complete installer and the 11-plug-in ZIP both include [Reverie 0.6.1](https://github.com/hdslave/hdslave-Reverie-Synth/releases/tag/v0.6.1). New tracks start on **Velvet Night**, the first of 46 original progressions. For an existing track, open **Stage → Chords**, set **Mood** to **Off**, set **Bank** to **Original**, and turn **Prog**. All 18 Mood overrides retain their voicings. Both downloads include an updated plug-in manifest and SHA-256 checksum.

## Changes in 0.8.2-hdslave.3

On Anvil’s STEPS panel, K1 and K2 now take over the pitch and velocity of the selected step. A small turn starts from that step’s value in Scaled mode. Knob takeover also follows edits made with the data wheel. The fix is in hdslaveOS and applies to plug-in panels that reassign a knob. To get it on an existing installation, install the OS-only ZIP or the complete installer.

The release also includes the Deep Freeze playback fix for tempo changes during unloading and the dark selection edge in Settings. The collection includes Slink 0.6.1 and Reverie 0.6.1 with its restored Original progression bank. Existing projects keep their plug-in paths.

hdslaveOS is based on Melodee 0.8.2 by Kerem Kiliç (Ellic Studio). The unsigned MPC build passed the ARM64 software tests, including Scaled, Pickup and Instant takeover. The Anvil check used the packaged host and plug-in. Physical MPC confirmation of the fix is pending.

The source tag pins sample-base and ellic-core. The plug-in archives include their licences and the source revisions and SHA-256 hashes for all eleven plug-ins in `MPC-PLUGINS.tsv`.

releases.name: MPC Remote addin v1.4.1
releases.body:
**Installer update for MPC OS 3.10.1.** The addin is unchanged from 1.4.0; only the bundled installer is new (open-mpc/mpc-vst-plugins at dbe1f2b).

- Fixes "Read-only file system" under `/etc/systemd/system/acvs.service.d/` when installing or updating on 3.10.1.
- **Gen1 with Akai's user access on (e.g. Key 37):** `/etc` is a read-only overlay stacked on a writable one; the drop-in is written in the writable layer and persists across reboots (open-mpc/mpc-vst-plugins#834).
- **Gen2 (e.g. Live III):** `/etc` is read-only, so the addin loads through a `/run` drop-in. `/run` is cleared at every reboot; the **Addin Restore** patch (Plugin Manager → PATCHES) puts it back at start-up.

Already have Remote? Reinstall it (Plugin Manager or the installer app): an addin installed from an older release keeps its older installer.

---

The MPC screen in a browser, and an MCP server so an AI model can see and touch it, play MIDI and read files.

## Requirements

- A Gen2 MPC OS standalone device (aarch64: Live III, One G2, Key(s) G2). The installer refuses anything else.
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit.
- Installing addins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.

## Install

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the device, e.g. `scp -r MPC-Remote-addin-1.4.1 root@<device-ip>:/tmp/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /tmp/MPC-Remote-addin-1.4.1/install.sh`

The installer copies the addin into `/data/mpc-addins/remote/`, adds `mpc_remote_addin.so` to the `LD_PRELOAD` list of MPC's service
and **restarts MPC** (save your project first). The list is extended, never replaced: other addins and the
libraries the firmware preloads stay. Where no writable file sets the list (the unit is on the read-only root), one
drop-in shared by every addin sets it, `/etc/systemd/system/<service>.service.d/90-mpc-addins.conf`. Re-run the
installer after a firmware update. `-y` skips the question, `-n` leaves the restart to you.

Settings are in `/data/mpc-addins/remote/mpc_remote_addin.conf`; an upgrade keeps your edits.

It listens on the device only. From your computer: ssh -L 6720:127.0.0.1:6720 root@<device address>, then open http://localhost:6720 (bind and port are in mpc_remote_addin.conf).

Uninstalling and the file list are in `INSTALL.md` inside each zip.

# MPC Sample draw handler addin 1.1.0

Owns the MPC Sample's screen for plugins that draw on it: the last plugin to ask gets the whole screen until it gives it back.

On the MPC Sample it now owns the screen for plugins and addins that draw on it; a long hold of PAD FX cycles their pages. Control (on the device): http://127.0.0.1:6740/status, /test?on=1 shows a test pattern, /release gives MPC its screen back. From a computer: ssh -L 6740:127.0.0.1:6740 root@<device address>.

## Uninstall

`ssh root@<device-ip> sh /data/mpc-addins/sample-draw-handler/uninstall.sh` takes the addin out of `LD_PRELOAD`, restarts MPC and

## Files

See `SHA256SUMS`. Made with [mpc-vst-plugins](https://github.com/open-mpc/mpc-vst-plugins) (`docs/ADDINS.md`).


## Changes in 1.1.0

- **MPC Sample 1.4:** 1.4 updates its screen with DRM atomic commits instead of page flips, so 1.0.1 drew nothing there.

- **API 4:** `list()` and `show_id()`, for pages that share a name (1.4 makes two instances of a pad's Knob FX). Older

releases.name: MPC Sample Scale Mode 1.2.0
releases.body:
**MPC Sample Scale Mode 1.2.0.** Hold 16 Levels (about a second) to turn Scale on or off; with Scale on, the 16 Levels slots play a scale, shown on the SCALE page.

Changes since 1.1.0:
- **The page is Scale.** A hold turns Scale and the SCALE page on together, and the next hold turns both off: MPC's screen comes straight back (it used to linger a few seconds, and closing the page with the dial left Scale on). A dial press now exits Scale too. If another page took the screen while Scale is on, a hold brings the SCALE page back.
- **Input lock.** While Scale is on, buttons and knobs no longer reach MPC, so nothing changes MPC's screen or parameters under the page (before, the knobs moved the sample's trim and other settings). The pads, 16 Levels, Shift, the transport (Rec, Overdub, Stop, Play, Play Start), notes 84-87 and the page's own keys, dial and K1-K3 still work. `lock_input=0` turns the lock off; `pass_notes` lists the buttons that get through. Each control kept from MPC is logged with its note.
- `padctl raw [n]` logs the raw control-surface input to MPC's journal.

Checked on an MPC Sample, firmware 1.3.0.12 (2026-11-09): the hold toggle and the input lock, by hand and with injected presses. Notes 84-87 are believed to be the bank buttons; not confirmed yet.

Needs [mpc-addin-sample-draw-handler](https://github.com/jacob-sabella/mpc-addin-sample-draw-handler) **1.0.1** or later for the page. The installer's `LD_PRELOAD` drop-in on the Sample is on `/run`, so reinstall after a reboot (or restore it from the SD card's autorun).

releases.name: MPC Sample Scale Mode 1.1.0
releases.body:
**MPC Sample Scale Mode** (was Enable Scale Mode). **Hold 16 Levels** (about a second) to turn Scale on or off. With Scale on, the 16 Levels slots play a scale instead of their usual steps. A short press is still a normal 16 Levels press, and Shift+16 Levels still cycles the Type.

![The SCALE page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jacob-sabella/mpc-addin-sample-scalemode/7f5c90324dbc6f3458eb17466a265d5992d2fade/docs/screenshots/scale-page.png)

Holding 16 Levels also opens a **SCALE page**. It shows the notes every slot plays and lights the one you hit; the soft keys pick scale, root or octave, the dial changes it, K1-K3 set them directly, and a dial press closes it. It stays up while Scale is on.

Needs [mpc-addin-sample-draw-handler](https://github.com/jacob-sabella/mpc-addin-sample-draw-handler) **1.0.1** or later for the page. Without it, the hold still toggles Scale.

**Upgrading from Enable Scale Mode 0.x:** the addin was renamed, so uninstall the old one first: `sh /data/mpc-addins/enable-scalemode/uninstall.sh`. While the old one is loaded, this one stays off and says so in MPC's log. Settings start fresh.

Changes since 1.0.0:
- **Always by ear.** `detect_pitch=always` (or `padctl detect always`) listens to every sample, not only untagged ones, and the note heard wins over the file's tag: for samples tagged with the wrong note. Checked on a Moog lead tagged D that sounds C#: with root A, slot 0 sounded G# by the tag and A by ear. A sample with no clear pitch keeps MPC's root note either way.
- `detect_pitch` takes `untagged` (the default, as in 1.0.0), `always` or `off` (0/1/2 still work); `padctl detect` shows or sets it and saves it to the conf.

Tested on an MPC Sample, firmware 1.3.0.12 (2026-11-06): the device test passes 19 of 19 from this zip, with every slot's pitch and the pad latency measured from the USB audio. The installer's `LD_PRELOAD` drop-in on the Sample is on `/run`, so reinstall after a reboot.

releases.name: RHYTHMER OS 0.2.0 — New sounds. Better flow.
releases.body:
# RHYTHMER OS 0.2.0
## New sounds. Better flow.

More sounds to explore, more direct editing, and a smoother path from your first note to a finished groove.

RHYTHMER OS 0.2.0 brings two new instruments, an updated FMini-1, refined Rhythmer Kit editing, and improvements throughout the track, Acid and Break workflows. Built for exploring Jungle, Techno, House and IDM on your MPC Sample.

### Meet your new instruments

- **Frodhes:** expressive electric pianos, vibraphone and marimba, with 57 original factory programs.
- **Tenebrae:** eight oscillator models spanning basses, leads, pads, keys and more, with 164 programs including Init.
- **FMini-1:** updated to the original 2.6.0 engine, with revised filter response, contour shaping and optimizations, retaining its 200 original factory presets.

### Start a track. Change direction.

TRACK SETUP brings instrument replacement, track types, MPC kit loading and track deletion into one visible menu. Change an instrument or track type while keeping your patterns; delete a track through its separate confirmation.

Press the encoder on an engine-less track to choose its type. On a Sample Kit, pressing it on an empty pad opens sample loading for that pad, including when the whole kit is empty. On-screen hints show the next step.

Change instruments directly from the preset list. Switch tracks while browsing and the screen follows the selected track. Preset browsing wraps from the last sound back to the first, in both directions.

B2 SENDS stays visible in BASIC. Its confirmation can enable FULL and open SENDS directly, or cancel without changing modes. Existing repeat-rate, MOVE/COPY and back controls retain their priority.

### Find a break. Keep the groove.

Browse loops with ORIGINAL or tempo-synchronised SYNC audition before loading them. Replacing a source preserves your existing patterns and performance settings, with clear confirmation when changing the source's bar count.

BREAK GEN and BRK PERF have clearer entry, return and loading controls. Pattern Hold, CHOP, LOOP and STRETCH have more explicit operating hints, while Variation and Stretch feedback show when the performance actions are active.

Loop audition remains separate from the track's musical state, so you can explore another source while keeping your current groove intact.

### Your pad. Your sound.

Rhythmer Kit's EDIT list starts with the selected pad's native **Volume**, followed by its supported Pan, Tune or Decay controls. Related parameters stay together in rows of three, with the whole-kit filter on the next row.

P01–P16 labels identify the pad you are editing; ALL PADS identifies the kit-wide filter. The 36 complete sixteen-pad factory kits retain their mixed-engine flexibility, pad-source replacement and User Kit saving.

Mute individual Rhythmer Kit pads with MUTE + pad, solo a pad with SHIFT + pad in mute mode, and clear project mutes with SHIFT + MUTE. Pad LEDs show the state, which is kept in the project without changing the kit's sound settings. TRACKS retains whole-track mute. Existing release and effect tails decay naturally.

### Shape it. Save it. Come back to it.

Parameter names and ordering are refined across oscillator, filter, envelope, LFO, modulation and effects controls. Source, Destination and Amount stay together, and named choices make settings such as Key Tracking and Polarity easier to read.

Open SAVE SOUND or PAD SOURCE from EDIT, save to one of 64 User Sound or User Kit slots, and reload your sounds from the preset list—even in another project. Save the project separately to keep its patterns and arrangement.

### Save where you choose

First SAVE and SAVE AS let you choose a folder and name. Further SAVE presses update that file. Opening another project or starting NEW offers SAVE, DISCARD or CANCEL instead of automatically overwriting your manual save.

Idle autosave updates one separate recovery entry per project under Rhythmer/Autosave. On the Project home screen, SHIFT + B3 RECOVERY opens the list; load a recovered copy and SAVE it deliberately.

### Build a chord progression

CHORD GEN is a separate instrument-track generator alongside the existing GENERATE Tn / MUTATE Tn workflow. Choose a genre, progression family, 1–8 chord changes and 1–16 bars; adjust rhythmic density, chord complexity, energy, voicing and register, then play the result as Block chords, an arpeggio or a strum.

It follows the project's key and scale by default. Local overrides affect only the generated part. Jazz and neo-soul profiles add extended harmony and voice leading. NEW CHORDS chooses another progression; MUTATE CHORDS keeps the progression while varying articulation. Generation keeps the instrument and other tracks, with Undo/Redo.

Rhythmer Kit retains genre-based drum generation; Acid and Break keep their dedicated generators. The illustrated manual and First Groove guide explain which command to use and how to return from each page.

### Acid, ready to play

Acid GEN keeps its NEW/MUTATE generation behavior while presenting its musical settings across two pages, without exposed seed controls.

Eight original Aphex choices join the Hortator Acid palette: **Acid Squelch, Lead Scream, Whistle Lead, Resonant Spike, Acid Seq, Reso Bass, Filter Cry and Techno Pulse**. Their native sound controls remain available for editing.

### Refinements

A steadier external MIDI BPM display keeps whole-number tempos clean while retaining meaningful fractional readings. The actual sync algorithm is unchanged. Rhythmer Kit animation flows across pad changes, and contextual Note Repeat and ARP controls remain available.

### Fixes

- Preset loading, parameter mapping, pad labels and state restoration.
- Track navigation, Back, confirmation, loading cancellation and Undo/Redo.
- Break playback, performance controls and held-command handling.
- User Sound/User Kit saving and error feedback.

### Make your first groove

The manual and **Your first groove with RHYTHMER OS.** guide cover the current navigation, track types, sound saving, independent Chord GEN and the Break workflow, with visual controls and step-by-step instructions.

[Download & Installation](https://jazzyrhythmer.github.io/mpc-sample/installer/) · [Manual](https://jazzyrhythmer.github.io/mpc-sample/manual/) · [Your first groove](https://jazzyrhythmer.github.io/mpc-sample/manual/quickstart.html)

RHYTHMER OS remains early beta software. Back up your SD card before installing, follow the installation guide, and keep sharing what feels good and what could work better.

Built on Melodee by Kerem Kiliç / Ellic Studio, with thanks to the original engine developers and open-source contributors. Original authorship, licenses and credits are retained.

**RHYTHMER OS — by Jazzy Rhythmer**

*In search of feel-good rhythms.*

## Workflow

- On native Sample Kit SOUND/TRIM, encoder Push opens TRACK TYPE if all 128 pads and layers are empty. SAMPLE KIT starts first-sample loading. If other pads contain samples, Push opens SAMPLES for the selected empty pad. Screen hints show both routes.
- Loaded/layered pads, other editors, recording/Freeze guards, Break loop entry and contextual Note Repeat controls keep their existing jobs. Shift + Push cancels the browser; B1 goes up folders or exits at the root. Sample load Undo preserves other pads.

## Acid Engine

The four original Hortator Acid sounds are retained. Eight unmodified Aphex factory choices are also available: **Acid Squelch, Lead Scream, Whistle Lead, Resonant Spike, Acid Seq, Reso Bass, Filter Cry and Techno Pulse**. They use the original Aphex DSP, native filters and source edit parameters. Source identity and edits persist in projects and User Sound; Rhythmer Kit pad source/restore is also covered.

## Validation

ARM64 build; 19 runtime unit tests; 290 track/input/navigation assertions; GEN/Acid/Break integration; audio self-test; 36,000 random surface moves; 430 UI previews with no text issues. Host regressions cover single instruments, 36 kits, engine/kit filters and 4,587 control round trips. releases.name: RHYTHMER OS 0.2.0-beta.3 — Break workflow hotfix.2
releases.body:
RHYTHMER OS for MPC Sample — 0.2.0-beta.3 / Break workflow hotfix.2.

The release version is **0.2.0-beta.3**. This separate release record identifies the matching installation files and corresponding source. The Sound / Kit save hotfix is included.

## Break: load, find the controls, play

- Loading or reloading source A makes a straight sixteen-chop pattern and stays in **BREAK GEN**, with **BRK PERF** selected. Push / B3 OPEN enters the performance pages.
- While decoding, **B1 CANCEL** or **SHIFT + encoder Push** cancels track assignment. Other generator actions and knob cards wait until loading finishes. A cached decoded file may remain; a cancelled request cannot replace the track.
- Source A/B completion does not reopen a dismissed menu or pull you away from another track. Replacing/deleting the target track continues to invalidate pending loads.
- Reopen controls from the Break track: **SEQ / PATTERNS → SHIFT + B3 GEN → BREAK GEN → BRK PERF**. In BRK PERF, B1 GEN returns to BREAK GEN. BACK / Shift + Push returns to main GEN, then closes it.
- **Pattern Hold** replaces the misleading LOOP HOLD label. It holds the internal generated pattern in LOOP mode, not audio sustain or track Freeze. The stored parameter and DSP behavior are unchanged. CHOP mode and zero variation can make the difference inaudible.
- Grain / Splice / Slow explicitly describe stretched hits. With playback running, hold Pad 3 STRETCH on ROLLS, keep it held while paging to GRAIN, adjust the controls and release; recorded STRETCH works too. Pattern Hold is not required.
- Rejected/undecodable files return to the owned browser for retry without replacing the previous instrument. A track frozen during decoding cancels assignment without a late Unfreeze dialog.
- All six pages have clearer operating hints. SOURCE B requires a loaded B file; TRACK MIX changes the track mix rather than generating a pattern. RETURN clears Variation/Drift while keeping the selected A/B source.
- General GEN also saves the Acid RNG stream with its Undo/Redo operation, keeping the generated notes and random state together. The generation algorithm and seed policy are unchanged.

## Install and learn

Use the **full SD ZIP**, verify its SHA-256 and back up the entire card first. The signed UPDATE ZIP is app-only and is not a first-install package; the native updater may not offer a same-version hotfix. Target: MPC Sample AC50 / stock firmware 1.3.0.12. No break recordings are bundled.

[Download & installation](https://jazzyrhythmer.github.io/mpc-sample/installer/) · [Break navigation and six-page guide](https://jazzyrhythmer.github.io/mpc-sample/manual/#break-performance) · [Your first groove](https://jazzyrhythmer.github.io/mpc-sample/manual/quickstart.html#break-load)

The written manual and first-groove guide now match this hotfix. The existing tutorial film predates the load/menu change; its music and edited arrangement remain examples. Follow the current written navigation when screens differ. Random generation does not reproduce the edited example exactly.

## Validation scope

Software checks cover cancellation, A/B async ownership, current-track navigation, Undo/Redo, project save/reload, held STRETCH release after paging, CHOP/LOOP pattern hold, grain processing, existing track workflows, runtime tests, audio self-test, random surface inputs and native UI text/layout. Exact results and source identity are recorded in the validation receipt. Current software results: 19 runtime tests, 161 track-workflow assertions, three final fresh-process GEN/Acid/Break passes, 430 standard UI states with zero reported text issues, 12 × 3,000 random surface inputs, 16 original roll commands and 2,400 Acid reference cases. All 41 plug-in binaries and eight sample files are unchanged. Engine DSP, preset banks and serialized control IDs remain unchanged from the prior reviewed hotfix. Signatures, archive checksums and corresponding-source files are checked before publication.

releases.name: MPCTRACKER 0.1.0
releases.body:
First release of MPCTRACKER, a pattern tracker for the Akai MPC Sample that runs from an SD card.

It has eight tracks and 64 sample slots, and it uses the ProTracker effect column. It loads WAV files and 4 to 8 channel .mod files, saves songs to the card, and starts with a short VHS style intro that any pad skips. The README has the full list of controls.

## Installing

1. Read the Safety section of the README, save the project that is open on the sampler and back up the card.
2. Unzip `mpctracker-v0.1.0-sd-card.zip` and copy the `autorun` and `tracker` folders to the root of the SD card. This replaces any `autorun` folder that is already on the card.
3. Put WAV files in `tracker/samples`, or browse to samples that are already on the card.
4. Insert the card. The tracker starts a few seconds after the sampler has booted.
5. Hold SHIFT and press STOP to quit back to the sampler. Take the card out and power cycle for a normal boot.

## Notes

This was developed against the emulator on firmware 1.3.0.12. It starts and plays sound on a real unit, but most of the hardware testing is still to do, so expect rough edges. It never touches the sampler's internal storage and it only writes inside the `tracker` folder on the card.

The zip has no demo song. A first run plays a built-in drum kit and groove. Copy a `.mod` file into `tracker/songs` before the first start and it opens that instead.

Still to come are sampling from the inputs, block copy and paste, a fill tool, naming songs on the device, a view of all eight tracks at once, and MIDI.

## Changed: read this first

- **The mixer opens on the strips.** Every channel of the row is a strip side by side: all 16 tracks, or the submixes, buses, input and master. Each strip shows its number, a stereo meter, its fader and **M** or **S** when on. The selected channel's strip is lit.
- **Hold + for the card.** The selected channel's card (its sends, FX, EQ or compressor) opens as before. Hold **−** to go back to the strips. The strips slide and the selected one grows into the card.
- **− / + on the mixer act when you let go.** A tap still moves through the lit block.

releases.name: Melodee 0.8.1
releases.body:
Melodee 0.8.1 for the Akai MPC Sample: a 16-track groovebox that runs on the MPC in place of the stock app, from the microSD card.

## Update

- **From 0.2.x to 0.8.0:** copy `Melodee-MPC-Sample-v0.8.1.zip` to the card, or send it from the web page at http://melodee.local. Melodee asks *Update to v0.8.1?*, saves, installs and restarts. On firmware 1.4.0.7 this works from 0.6.6.
- **Firmware 1.4.0.8:** 0.7.1 and earlier do not start on it. Update Melodee first, then the firmware. Already on 1.4.0.8: install by hand as in [Install](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample#install): turn on **Developer Mode**, unzip, and copy the `autorun` folder and the `autorun.sh` file to the top level of the card. Moving from 1.3.0.12 to 1.4, copy the zip's `autorun.sh` to the top level of the card too.
- **On firmware 1.4.0.7 from 0.6.5 or earlier, from 0.1.0, or a new card:** install by hand as in [Install](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample#install).
- **With SampleBoot:** replace Melodee's folder in `autorun/mods/` with the zip's `autorun` folder.

Requires an MPC Sample on firmware **1.3.0.12**, **1.4.0.7** or **1.4.0.8**.

Back up `Melodee/Projects` before you update.

## Fixed

- **Echo and reverb tails.** An effect plug-in that reports a tail keeps running for that tail after its last sound, up to 10 seconds, instead of stopping after half a second of silence. Echoes with long gaps between repeats play out. A tail that a preset changes counts from the change.
- **Presets on a plug-in at rest.** A preset picked on **PRESETS** for a sleeping CLAP plug-in takes effect at once, without waiting for a note.
- **A sustain pedal left down** no longer keeps a plug-in instrument running in silence: All Sound Off (CC 120) and Reset All Controllers (CC 121) lift it.

## Faster

- The screen copies the kits and the pattern overviews only after a change, not for every frame (about 0.8 MB a frame before).
- Plug-ins take less work on every block: their load is measured on one block in 16, their output level while it is copied, and a CLAP plug-in's unused inputs are cleared once instead of every block.
- 32-bit VST2 plug-ins: when a plug-in takes longer than a short wait, Melodee sleeps until it answers instead of keeping a core busy. An idle plug-in no longer wakes ten times a second.
- The controls' lights no longer go through all 8,192 sample slots every 5 ms.

releases.name: Melodee 0.8.0
releases.body:
Melodee 0.8.0 for the Akai MPC Sample: a 16-track groovebox that runs on the MPC in place of the stock app, from the microSD card.

## Update

- **From 0.2.x to 0.7.1:** copy `Melodee-MPC-Sample-v0.8.0.zip` to the card, or send it from the web page at http://melodee.local. Melodee asks *Update to v0.8.0?*, saves, installs and restarts. On firmware 1.4.0.7 this works from 0.6.6.
- **Firmware 1.4.0.8:** 0.7.1 and earlier do not start on it. Update Melodee first, then the firmware. Already on 1.4.0.8: install by hand as in [Install](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample#install): turn on **Developer Mode**, unzip, and copy the `autorun` folder and the `autorun.sh` file to the top level of the card. Moving from 1.3.0.12 to 1.4, copy the zip's `autorun.sh` to the top level of the card too.
- **On firmware 1.4.0.7 from 0.6.5 or earlier, from 0.1.0, or a new card:** install by hand as in [Install](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample#install).
- **With SampleBoot:** replace Melodee's folder in `autorun/mods/` with the zip's `autorun` folder.

Requires an MPC Sample on firmware **1.3.0.12**, **1.4.0.7** or **1.4.0.8**.

Back up `Melodee/Projects` before you update. Projects from earlier versions open as they were: each track keeps its level, pan and sends, and its new strip starts flat.

## Changed: read this first

- **The mixer replaces Tracks and Sends.** **PAD FX** + **KNOB FX** opens the new mixer (see below). The Menu's pad 10 (**SENDS**) is empty.
- **Stage's MIX and SENDS are gone.** A track's level, pan and sends are on the mixer; **B3** on Stage is **FX**. On a kit, **B3** still has **SENDS** for the pads' own sends; the kit's own sends (**KIT SEND**) are on the mixer.
- **Track speed** is on Patterns: **SHIFT** + **K3** (**SPEED**). It was **SHIFT** + **K1** on Tracks. The metronome level, which **SHIFT** + **K3** set there before, is on Tempo.
- **CPU:** the Menu's header shows how much of the processor the tracks use and the selected track's share. Tracks showed it per track.
- **Plug-in tracks have no separate Edit page.** Picking a plug-in opens Stage on **EDIT**, the third page under **B1**; a plug-in's own screen is **PANEL**, the page before. Hold **SHIFT** on a **B1** page for the plug-in's keys: **B1** (**PLUG-INS**) the picker, **B2** (**PRESETS**) the preset list, **B3** (**TRANSPORT**) whether it hears Play and Stop.

## New

### Mixer

- Press **PAD FX** and **KNOB FX** together, or pad 9 (**MIXER**) on the Menu's **GO**. The selected channel is the wide card in the middle with its meter, fader, pan, **M** and **S**; its neighbours are narrow strips with their meters and faders. Pads select a channel, the encoder brings the next one to the middle, the fader sets its level.
- Every track plays through its effect chain, then its **strip**: trim, a nine-band EQ, a compressor and width. Then its level and pan.
- **B1** (**SENDS**): sends A–C on **K1**–**K3**; **+** for pan, output and send D. **B1** again (**FX**): the channel's effect chain in the card. Push edits the lit effect on its FX page, **MUTE** turns it off or on, **ERASE** removes it, **SHIFT** + **ERASE** copies it, and Push on the **+** opens the effect picker.
- **B2** (**EQ**): nine bands, 63 Hz to 16 kHz, ±12 dB, drawn as a curve. **K1**–**K3** set three at a time; **B2** again for the next three. Behind the curve is what the channel plays now.
- **B3** (**COMP**): **K1** amount, **K2** ratio, **K3** speed; **SHIFT**: key, mix, gain. The picture shows the curve with the sound on it and the gain reduction.
- **Eight submixes.** **OUTPUT** (**SENDS**, second row) sends a track to the master or to submix 1–8. A submix has its own chain, strip, level, pan, mute, solo and four sends; its solo solos the tracks in it.
- **PAD BANK** shows the second row: the submixes on pads 1–8, the buses A–D on pads 9–12, the input on pad 15 and the master on pad 16. Each has an EQ and a compressor; buses and the master have their chains.
- **The input** (pad 15): **B1** (**INPUT**) **K1** trim, **K2** monitor (**OFF**, **AUTO**, **ON**), **K3** record **DRY** or **WET**: takes before or after the input's strip.
- **The master** (pad 16): **B3** is the master compressor, as **SHIFT** + **Pad 5**.
- In mute mode, a pad mutes its channel and **SHIFT** + pad solos it. Pads light in their channel's colour, as bright as its level.
- **SHIFT** + **KNOB FX** opens the selected channel's full effect page; **B1** (**MIXER**) comes back.
- With **SEQ RECORD** on, the selected track's level, pan, sends and strip are recorded as Motion lanes.
- **Pad outputs.** As on MPC 3, a kit pad can play into a submix instead of the kit: on the kit's Stage **SENDS** page, hold **SHIFT** and turn **K2** (**OUTPUT**), **KIT** or **SUB 1**–**SUB 8**. The pad goes there after its own effects, volume and pan, at the kit's level, pan and mute. **STEMS** puts it in the submix's WAV, and an **MPC 3** export sends it to the same submix. A kit with pads sent to submixes cannot be frozen.
- In Basic, the mixer has **SENDS** with send A and pan.
- See [The mixer](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/blob/main/docs/guide/mixer-and-effects.md#the-mixer).

### USB out

- **Settings** (**AUDIO**) > **USB out** chooses what a computer records on inputs 3 to 18 after the mix: **Tracks** (as before: tracks 1–16, one mono input each) or **Submixes** (submixes 1–8 in stereo, 3–4 submix 1 up to 17–18 submix 8). Changing it keeps the computer connected.

### Export

- **STEMS writes each kit pad apart.** Each pad the song plays gets a WAV of its own, in a folder for each kit beside the kit's own WAV: `03 Drums pads/A01 Kick.wav`. A pad's WAV is the pad after its own effects, volume and pan, at the kit's level, pan and mute; with no effects or strip on the kit, its pads add up to the kit's WAV. A silent pad gets none, a frozen kit's pads are not split. When there are more stems than one play of the song can write to the card, **STEMS** plays the song again for the rest of the pads (*Stems: pass 2 of 3*), with the same hits.
- **STEMS** also writes one WAV for each submix the tracks play into, named after the submix.
- Stems are written to the card in large blocks from a thread of their own, so more of them keep up as the song plays.
- An **MPC 3** export sends each track to the same submix in MPC 3, with the submix's level, pan, mute and solo.
- **MPC 3** and **LIVE SET** exports say *mixer settings left out* when the project has mixer settings they cannot carry, such as the strips.
- See [Export](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/blob/main/docs/guide/song.md#export).

### Plug-ins

- **Companion screens.** A VST2 plug-in can get a page of its own without changing the plug-in: copy a screen's folder into `Melodee/Plugin Screens/` on the card, beside the plug-in as it was released. It shows on Stage's **PANEL** when the plug-in has no screen of its own. Melodee checks that every parameter the screen uses is where it expects and otherwise shows its own pages, with the reason in `Melodee/Plugin Screens/problems.txt`. The screen runs in a process of its own: one that stops working is closed, Melodee's pages come back and the plug-in plays on. Projects never need the screen. See [A screen installed apart from the plug-in](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/blob/main/docs/guide/plug-ins.md#a-screen-installed-apart-from-the-plug-in); screen makers: [Companion screens](https://github.com/keremimo/melodee-sample/blob/main/docs/PLUGIN_COMPANIONS.md).
- A CLAP plug-in whose preset locations have a `/` in their names lists them as folders on **PRESETS**.

### Browsing

- **The browsers start at the top of the card.** The first time you open the sample browser or the project list, it opens at the top of the card, where most keep their own folders, instead of in Melodee's own `Melodee/Samples` or `Melodee/Projects`. After that it opens where you left it. The sample browser keeps a folder for kits, keygroups, audio tracks and the rest apart. The project list still opens on the open project the first time.

### Firmware 1.4.0.8

- Melodee runs and starts from the card on firmware 1.4.0.8, as on 1.4.0.7: turn on **Developer Mode** and press Yes when the stock app asks to run the card's autorun script.

releases.name: sample-base v0.1.0 — demos proof of concept (no SSH)
releases.body:
A proof of concept of sample-base's demos that starts from the microSD card: no computer, SSH or network connection needed.

**Requires MPC Sample firmware 1.3.0.12 exactly.** On anything else the demos do not start and the stock app keeps running.

### Install
1. Back up the card. Move any existing top-level `autorun` folder (MPC Sample Plugins, Melodee) somewhere safe: this one replaces it.
2. Copy the `autorun` folder from the zip to the top level of the card. Don't edit or rename anything inside: the MPC refuses an autorun whose files changed.
3. Switch the MPC on. The stock app starts first; a few seconds later the demos take over the screen.

**Push the wheel** to go back to stock until the next boot. Delete the `autorun` folder to uninstall. A crash or failed start also brings stock back; nothing on the MPC itself changes, only the card.

### What's in it
- Pads play a 16-voice sine/triangle synth in C major; external MIDI plays it too
- **Sample**: record Line in, Mic or USB-C for up to 60 s and play it back
- **Pad FX**: a light show over every LED on the surface
- **16 Levels**: pad velocity and pressure
- **SEQ**: eight-drum, sixteen-step sequencer
- **Knob FX**: live system dashboard

### Files
`sample-base-demos-MPC-Sample-v0.1.0.zip`, SHA256 `d338960d4eb3b8d9129b7ba3e513fe1fbda6d455081a00d21ddb0003ca576652` (also in the `.sha256` asset). Built from 34f8fc7. AGPL-3.0-only, JUCE under AGPLv3; licences are in the zip. Not affiliated with inMusic or Akai Professional.

releases.name: USB DeClick v0.1.0 Beta 1
releases.body:
# USB DeClick v0.1.0-beta.1 — First Public Beta

**Experimental USB click-reduction patch for Akai MPC Sample, tested with Google Pixel 8a (Android 16).**

USB DeClick reduces recurring, sharp digital clicks that can occur when sampling a phone's audio over USB. It runs on the MPC from an SD card, without an Android companion app or permanent firmware modification.

## What this beta includes

- **Real-time PCM click repair** that tracks a recurring 10 ms spike pattern and corrects strong, isolated stereo impulses using neighboring audio frames.
- **Manual ON/OFF control.** Edit `autorun/USB_DECLICK_MODE.txt` before startup. `ON` enables repair. With `OFF`, the MPC application starts without modification.
- **Targeted USB capture processing** for the MPC's 44.1 kHz, stereo, 32-bit USB audio input.
- **Fixed-size audio state** with no filesystem writes from the PCM processing loop. Long-term CPU and RAM usage on the MPC still need measurement.
- **Removable SD-card installation** with rollback by restarting the MPC without the mod card.
- **Monochrome startup screen** showing that the mod was launched.

## Test evidence

The issue was investigated on a **Google Pixel 8a (Android 16)** connected to an **Akai MPC Sample (firmware 1.3.0.12)**. Recordings showed isolated stereo sample spikes following a **441-frame / 10 ms pattern** at 44.1 kHz.

In a controlled comparison of approximately one-minute recordings of the same track at similar volume, the detector found the following counts.

| Without repair | With repair |
| ---: | ---: |
| 1,335 strong-spike candidates | 25 strong-spike candidates |

The detector found **approximately 98.1% fewer strong-spike candidates** in this comparison. The test used a development build with the same audio repair core as this beta. The beta produced qualitatively similar results on the MPC. A separate controlled benchmark for this beta is still pending.

Some audible artifacts may remain, and results may vary across devices. See the [research findings](https://github.com/odeo0/usb-declick-mpc-sample/blob/86ecbf69e1d3e96c87044a023b5431991b8ccfcb/docs/research-findings.md) and [reproducible test methodology](https://github.com/odeo0/usb-declick-mpc-sample/blob/86ecbf69e1d3e96c87044a023b5431991b8ccfcb/docs/testing-method.md).

## Device support

**The Pixel 8a is the only affected phone tested so far.** A Samsung Galaxy A06 and a laptop produced clean control recordings on the same MPC. Compatibility with other affected phones remains unverified. Reports from other devices are welcome.

## Installation and safety

Download the **SD install ZIP** attached to this release and follow the [installation guide](https://github.com/odeo0/usb-declick-mpc-sample/blob/86ecbf69e1d3e96c87044a023b5431991b8ccfcb/INSTALL.md).

The repair is experimental. Some clicks may remain, and `ON` may alter genuine sharp musical transients. Use `OFF` when repair is unnecessary. To switch modes, edit the mode file and reboot. There is no on-screen toggle. Keep this installation separate from other autorun modifications.

**To roll back**, power off the MPC, remove the mod SD card, and reboot. Installation leaves the internal firmware intact.

## Help improve it

Share your phone and MPC models, firmware, test conditions, `ON` or `OFF` setting, and, if possible, two recordings of the same passage. Use the [community test report template](https://github.com/odeo0/usb-declick-mpc-sample/blob/86ecbf69e1d3e96c87044a023b5431991b8ccfcb/docs/community-test-report.md).

**Unofficial experimental beta. No affiliation with or endorsement by Akai.**

## MPC Mix 0.1.0 beta 1

Native iPhone editor and mixer for Akai MPC Sample firmware **1.3.0.12**.

releases.name: SampleBoot 1.0.2
releases.body:
One card, every OS: a boot selector for the Akai MPC Sample. Website: https://sampleboot.com

## Added

- **`sampleboot.inplace`.** An empty file with this name in a system's folder makes SampleBoot run it from `autorun/` itself, as if it were alone on the card. For systems that take "the folder above their own" for the card. **MPCTRACKER 0.1.0 needs it**: without it, its file browser stays inside `autorun/mods/` and it looks for its songs and samples there.
- **Boot history.** `autorun/sampleboot/boot-history.log` keeps the logs of the last 10 boots, each headed by its date, to compare tests. `BOOT_HISTORY` in `sampleboot.conf` sets how many (0 = none).
- **[Notes for OS authors](https://github.com/pxcm/SampleBoot/blob/main/docs/OS-AUTHORS.md):** how to make a system that runs from SampleBoot exactly as it runs on its own.

## Fixed

- The last line of `last-boot.log` could be missing when the card was read from a computer through SD card access without a restart. It is now written to the card at once.

## Works with

Firmware 1.3.0 (1.3.0.12) with SampQOL OS 0.1.4.7 to 0.3.0, Melodee 0.1.0 to 0.3.0, MPC Simple 1.0 Beta 1 to Beta 3 and MPCTRACKER 0.1.0 (tested), ODDFORM 1.2.0 beta (reported by a user). See the [list](https://github.com/pxcm/SampleBoot#works-with).

## Updating

Copy the `autorun` folder from the zip over the one on your card (your systems in `autorun/mods/` stay), or run `tools/add_mod.py` with your card's path to keep your settings too. A `sampleboot.conf` from 1.0.x works as it is.

releases.name: SampleBoot 1.0.1
releases.body:
One card, every OS: a boot selector for the Akai MPC Sample.

## Fixed

- **SampQOL OS 0.3.0's 16 USB audio outputs now work when SampQOL is started from SampleBoot.** SampQOL keeps its settings in `mpcqol.conf` at the card root, but its start script reads them from the folder above its own, which under SampleBoot is `autorun/mods/`. SampleBoot now shows the card root's `mpcqol.conf` in `autorun/mods/` too (a bind mount of that one file, until power-off), so SampQOL reads its real settings. The first time, a copy of the file is left in `autorun/mods/`: that's expected.

## Added

- `ROOT_FILES` setting in `sampleboot.conf`: the settings files to show in `autorun/mods/` this way. Default `"mpcqol.conf"`.

## Tested

Firmware 1.3.0 (1.3.0.12) with Melodee 0.1.0 to 0.3.0, SampQOL OS 0.1.4.7 to 0.3.0 and MPC Simple 1.0 Beta 1 and Beta 2.

## Updating from 1.0.0

Copy the `autorun` folder from the zip over the one on your card (your systems in `autorun/mods/` stay), or run `tools/add_mod.py` with your card's path to keep your settings. A `sampleboot.conf` from 1.0.0 works as it is: the default applies.

Thanks to the user who reported the missing USB outputs!

releases.name: MaiaOS - Beta V2
releases.body:
MaiaOS V2 for MPC Sample

MaiaOS V2 adds a horizontal Song timeline, stereo Master and experimental Stems export, external plug-in support, and two-deck DJ Mode. It runs from an exFAT microSD on MPC Sample with stock firmware 1.3.0.12. It requires no internal installation or SSH setup.

What's new

Song timeline and export — Arrange named sequences on a horizontal timeline and follow the playhead during playback. Open Song with Shift + Pad 12, then press B1 for Song Export. Choose Master for a stereo WAV or Stems for separate WAVs for Drums, Bass, Synths, and Melody Samples. Review and change pad assignments before rendering. Press the encoder in the main Song Export menu to combine the song into one editable MPC sequence. Audio exports go to the card's Export/ folder.

External plug-ins — Import VST2, VST3, LV2, and CLAP builds for Linux AArch64 as instruments or effects. The encoder switches parameter pages. Hold Shift for additional controls on supported pages. Instrument plug-ins work with 16 Levels and Chord Mode.

External MIDI — Play the selected sample or instrument pad chromatically, even with 16 Levels closed. REC and OVERDUB capture pitch, velocity, and note duration on that pad.

Sound editing — Three-band EQ and a spectrum display are available for samples, synths, Multisamples, and instrument plug-ins. For a sample pad, open Filter and press the encoder. Instrument screens have an oscilloscope, and Knob FX labels and values are larger.

DJ Mode — Load two decks with scrolling beatgrids, tempo sync, nudge, and loops. Press Sequence to choose stereo master on OUT 1/2 with stereo USB cue, or mono master on OUT 1 with mono cue on OUT 2. Pad FX works while the decks play. Flex Beat stays bypassed, and leaving DJ Mode requires confirmation.

Fixes

Switching pads closes the EQ editor and preserves each pad's settings. Returning to the original pad restores normal encoder navigation.

FIX: The microSD launcher and file browsers follow the mounted card when its volume is renamed.

Install from microSD

Extract the V2 ZIP and copy the entire autorun folder to the root of an exFAT microSD. The volume can have any name.

Power off the MPC, insert the card, and power on. When updating from an earlier build, replace the entire autorun folder.

To return to stock firmware, power off, remove the card, and power on again.

If startup fails, keep autorun/maia-boot.log if it was created. Use a fresh copy of autorun before retrying.

Known limitations

Stems export is experimental. Separate renders may differ from the full master, especially with compression, limiting, saturation, or sidechain processing. Audition the four WAVs before using them in another project.

External plug-ins are session-based. Reopening a project requires reloading the plug-ins and setting their parameters again.


The external plug-in host is based on Melodee by Kerem Kilic (Ellic Studio).

Use at your own risk, the developer decline any reponsibility over failed installation/crashes/bricks

snarebes/SampQOL-OS.description: SampQOL OS: a free SD-card mod for the Akai MPC Sample (firmware 1.3.0)

releases.name: SampQOL OS 0.4.2 (beta)
releases.body:
SampQOL OS is a free mod for the MPC Sample firmware 1.3.0 (1.3.0.12). It starts from the SD card and does not change the stock firmware. With the SD card in, it starts by itself. Without the SD card, the MPC starts as stock 1.3.0.

Tested only with MPC Sample 1.3.0. MPC One, Live and X are not tested yet. This is beta software: back up your projects first. A failed project load can delete samples (see the manual, "Project safety net").

## Fixed in 0.4.2

- Notes that you copy to another track play with the same timing. RT Swing (SEQ, K3) is one value for the whole sequence, for all drum tracks. Each track had its own RT Swing, so the copy played with a different swing (GitHub #95).
- 16 LEVELS in Scale, on a track with its own MIDI channel: the pad pressure (aftertouch) goes out on the note that plays. It went out on the pad's own note, a note that did not play. A synth could then keep a note playing after you let go of the pad.
- Load Kit loads a drum program (.xpm) that MPC 3.9 or newer saved. It showed "Only a drum program can load as a kit", also for a drum program. MPC 3.9 saves a .xpm in a new file format, with its WAV files in a folder next to it: for Boom Kit.xpm, the folder Boom Kit_[ProgramData]. As before, only the samples load.

## Known issues

- A project with a different time signature per sequence opens with one time signature for all sequences on a stock MPC Sample, and with Time Sig set to All.
- Without SampQOL OS (also on the MPC Live), the pad mutes of each sequence do not play. The pads have the mutes of the save in all sequences.
- Mute notes uses the probability of the note: a muted note has probability 0, and unmute sets it to 100 %. The MPC Sample has no probability, so you do not lose anything there. On an MPC with probability (MPC Live, One, X): a muted note shows 0 %, and a note that you mute and unmute on the MPC Sample loses its old probability.
- Without SampQOL OS (also on the MPC Live), a Chop Mode recording with Note On can stop a slice too early: at the end of the slice before it.

All features and the buttons that work differently: see the [README](https://github.com/snarebes/SampQOL-OS#readme). The [release notes](https://beatops.io/sampqol/changelog) have all changes from stock 1.3.0. Manual.html in the zip shows how to use each function.

## Install

1. Make sure that the MPC Sample has firmware 1.3.0. Start the MPC **without** the SampQOL card. Push **SHIFT** + **PAD 8** (MIDI Config). The top right of the display must show **v1.3.0**. The full version number is 1.3.0.12. The display shows only v1.3.0. This is the correct firmware. (When SampQOL OS runs, it shows the SampQOL OS version there.)
2. Download **SampQOL-OS-v0.4.2.zip** below and unzip it.
3. Copy the folder **autorun** to the root of an exFAT microSD card.
4. Turn off the MPC. Put the card in the MPC. Turn on the MPC.
5. SampQOL OS starts by itself. You do not push a button.

Update from an earlier version: replace the folder **autorun** on the card with the new one. Your settings stay: mpcqol.conf is on the top level of the card, not in the folder autorun.

Go back to stock: turn on the MPC without the card. To use the card on stock, rename the folder **autorun** (for example to **autorun-off**), or move it into a different folder on the card.

If the MPC hangs at start-up: hold the power button until the MPC goes off, then remove the card. See Troubleshooting in Manual.html.

releases.name: SampQOL OS 0.4.1 (beta)
releases.body:
SampQOL OS is a free mod for the MPC Sample firmware 1.3.0 (1.3.0.12). It starts from the SD card and does not change the stock firmware. With the SD card in, it starts by itself. Without the SD card, the MPC starts as stock 1.3.0.

Tested only with MPC Sample 1.3.0. MPC One, Live and X are not tested yet. This is beta software: back up your projects first. A failed project load can delete samples (see the manual, "Project safety net").

## Fixed in 0.4.1

- Save Sample and Save Project: Do It! (B3) shows the folder page again, so you can pick the folder and the drive. In 0.4.0 the page did not show: the first B3 seemed to do nothing, the second B3 saved into the default folder (Samples/User or Projects/User on Internal, or the Projects folder on the SD card), and after the first B3 the ENCODER seemed to stop working.
- Monitor On: from start-up, you hear the input without the Knob FX and the master effects. Before, you heard these effects on the input until you opened SAMPLE RECORD one time.
- Stems Separation: when the internal storage is too full, the screen tells you to save the project to the SD card and load it again. It showed only "Not enough space", without what to do.
- Stems Separation works with a sample name that holds " * : < > ? \ or |, and with a long sample name that has an accent (é, ü). The split failed: the SD card did not accept the stem file name. The stem names get "_" in place of these characters.
- Stems Separation: when a split file is missing on the SD card, the screen shows which file and where ("Not found: autorun/split/spl4h.bin"). It showed only "Split files missing".
- The mod screens show names with accents and other special characters (é, ü, ñ, €) correctly. "café" showed as "cafÃ©".
- Time Sig Per Seq: a loaded project gives each sequence the right length for its time signature. In 0.4.0 a sequence in for example 7/8 could load with the length of 4/4 bars, so it played too long.
- Pad View and Track View: each note of a pad shows as its own block. In 0.4.0 two notes side by side, or a note inside a long note, showed as one block, so you could not see the second note. In the Track View with very many notes, the last notes did not show.

## Fixed in 0.4.1 (stock problems)

- Resample: a second pad push on the "Select pad" screen does nothing. Stock started a second render, and the MPC froze on the progress bar.

## Known issues

- A project with a different time signature per sequence opens with one time signature for all sequences on a stock MPC Sample, and with Time Sig set to All.
- Without SampQOL OS (also on the MPC Live), the pad mutes of each sequence do not play. The pads have the mutes of the save in all sequences.
- Mute notes uses the probability of the note: a muted note has probability 0, and unmute sets it to 100 %. The MPC Sample has no probability, so you do not lose anything there. On an MPC with probability (MPC Live, One, X): a muted note shows 0 %, and a note that you mute and unmute on the MPC Sample loses its old probability.
- Without SampQOL OS (also on the MPC Live), a Chop Mode recording with Note On can stop a slice too early: at the end of the slice before it.

All features and the buttons that work differently: see the [README](https://github.com/snarebes/SampQOL-OS#readme). The [release notes](https://beatops.io/sampqol/changelog) have all changes from stock 1.3.0. Manual.html in the zip shows how to use each function.

## Install

See the README for the newest version. Manual.html in this zip has the install steps for this version.
